args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in production in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. It had also been unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Verified after the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and check why it was promoted even though staging was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Before:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback version:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. Change-manager approval wasn't needed, since that's only required for versions that have never been healthy in production.
- **After:** all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 covers what failed, the rollback and the post-rollback check. It also lists two follow-ups:
  - Find out why v2.3.1 failed before it's deployed again.
  - Check why it went to production even though its staging build (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy.
